sources.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics (complete author-hosted lecture notes, 2021 revision)
sources.locator: §2.2–§2.2.1 (classical ideal gas, canonical normalization, equipartition and speed distribution); §5.3.1 (the one-dimensional Ising transfer matrix and its finite-parameter eigenvalue gap). The retained prior source record documents the actual complete reading extent; broader one-dimensional no-transition claims are not imported.

contents.name: §2.2–§2.2.1: classical ideal gas partition, factorization, equipartition and speed law
contents.support: Independent statistical-mechanics treatment of the canonical ideal gas, its momentum Gaussian and speed law. The local theorem retains its own finite-dimensional derivation, explicit h0 reference and adopted 1/N! convention.

contents.name: §2.2.1: quadratic free-degree equipartition discussion
contents.support: The local theorem proves the positive-definite quadratic covariance directly and retains its explicit boundary and zero-mode limitations.

contents.name: §5.3.1: one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising transfer matrix and finite positive-temperature gap
contents.support: Supports the exact transfer-matrix interface; the local proof separately derives the spin-inserted finite-ring correlation formula and its fixed-distance limit.

contents.name: Broader source discussion of one-dimensional ordering outside the specified finite-range nearest-neighbor chain
contents.reason: The carrier is limited to the explicitly defined finite periodic nearest-neighbor Ising model; no general long-range or arbitrary one-dimensional phase claim is used.

sources.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 13 (Fall 2013)
sources.locator: Lecture 13, IV.D 'The Ideal Gas', printed pp. 79–82 (PDF pp. 1–4): microcanonical phase-space shell, Gaussian product, ideal-gas energy and momentum marginal; IV.E, printed pp. 82–84 (PDF pp. 4–6): indistinguishable-particle counting convention.

contents.name: IV.D: Gaussian product and finite microcanonical momentum sphere
contents.support: Supplies an independent classical microcanonical and Gaussian reference treatment. The local result is the explicitly chosen normalized spherical pushforward and proves its exact block marginal without identifying it with every shell measure.

contents.name: IV.D–IV.E: classical ideal-gas phase-space normalization and identical-particle factor
contents.support: Provides a second independent ideal-gas treatment; the local item declares h0 and the 1/N! convention as model inputs rather than deriving indistinguishability from mechanics.

contents.name: Large-N Maxwell approximation to a finite shell marginal
contents.reason: The current theorem proves an exact finite-N marginal and a fixed-block bounded-Lipschitz limit directly; it does not use an uncontrolled Stirling approximation or claim finite-shell equality with the canonical law.

sources.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 14 (Fall 2013)
sources.locator: Lecture 14, IV.G 'Examples', printed pp. 89–91 (PDF pp. 2–4): canonical ideal gas; IV.I 'The Grand Canonical Ensemble', printed pp. 92–94 (PDF pp. 5–7): sector probabilities and ideal-gas grand partition function.

contents.name: IV.G–IV.I: canonical and grand-canonical ideal-gas preparations
contents.support: Independent comparison for canonical and grand-canonical formulas. The local proof evaluates the exponential sector sum and derives the Poisson law from its power series.

contents.name: IV.G–IV.I: ensemble conventions and grand-sector weighting
contents.support: Context for the explicitly adopted ensemble bridge; it is not evidence that any real system equilibrates or realizes these preparations.

sources.title: University of Warwick, PX439/CO904 Statistical Mechanics of Complex Systems, lecture notes
sources.locator: §3.5 'The Tonks gas: excluded volume', printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pp. 27–28): ordered hard-rod configuration integral, free volume and pressure formula.

contents.name: §3.5: exact one-dimensional Tonks hard-rod configuration integral and equation of state
contents.support: An independent hard-rod treatment agrees after identifying its excluded length l0=2a for rods of length a. The local proof derives the ordered simplex volume and gives an exact finite-N virial remainder.

contents.name: §3.5–§4 approximate two-dimensional rod ordering discussion
contents.reason: The carrier proves only the exact one-dimensional Tonks model; no higher-dimensional ordering or phase-transition claim is included.

sources.title: Michael E. Taylor, Introduction to Analysis in Several Variables (Advanced Calculus), §3.1
sources.locator: §3.1, printed pp. 105–107 (PDF pp. 117–119), equations (3.1.72)–(3.1.75): polar evaluation of the plane Gaussian, product integral, and n-dimensional Gaussian normalization; Theorem 3.1.9 on compact-set change of variables.

contents.name: §3.1, equations (3.1.72)–(3.1.75): Gaussian integral and finite products
contents.support: Independent analysis treatment of the Gaussian normalization and finite product calculation used by the local compact-exhaustion proof.

contents.name: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.9: compact-set change of variables
contents.support: Supports the stated calculus convention; the Jacobian identity itself is proved from the exact imported determinant, chain-rule, trace, mean-value and intermediate-value suppliers.

contents.name: §3.1 general multivariable integral theory beyond the explicitly used compact substitutions
contents.reason: No general coarea, measure-preserving-flow existence, or unlisted measure-theory result is imported from this chapter.

contents.name: §5.2(i), equation 5.2.1: gamma-function integral convention
